messages.subject: Re: kmeans issue [SEC=UNCLASSIFIED]
parts:
Hi Graham;

The dataset comes from the book, and can be found here: https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/datasets/Wholesale+customers#

After downloading the file and opening R and Rattle, in the "Data" tab I:
1. Select .csv file;
2. Upload .csv file using Execute;
3. Select "Ignore" for variables 1 Channel and 2 Region;
4. Execute;
5. In "Explore" tab I make sure "Summary" and "Summary" are both selected;
6. Execute.

That's when I find that Rattle has only "seen" 308 observations.

When I go to the "Cluster" tab, I: 

1. Select "KMeans", 
2. Number of clusters: 10; 
3. No Re-scale;
4. Select Iterate Clusters;
5. Execute;
The plot produced is different to the book because the peak is at 5 instead of 6, but I continue to follow the book and
6. Select Number of Clusters: 6;
7. Deselect Iterate Clusters
8. Select Runs: 10
9. Execute
10. Go to "Evaluate" tab
11. Select KMeans, Training, and All
This produces a .csv with a kmeans column filled for 308 rows.

I have downloaded the file a couple of times, but have not achieved any different results?

Thanks for your help, all the best,

John

Hi John,

On the Data tab you have Partition enabled. This is what Tony Nolan was referring to. By default Rattle will partition the dataset into train/evaluate/test with 70% chosen for the training dataset: 0.7 * 440 = 308. Uncheck the Partition option to use the whole dataset.

Regards,
Graham
